# Graham Priest — *The Fifth Corner of Four* (2018)

## Bibliographic identity

The selected object is Graham Priest, *The Fifth Corner of Four: An Essay on Buddhist Metaphysics and the Catuṣkoṭi* (Oxford: Oxford University Press, 2018); some printings carry 2019, and the copyright page must be checked before the year is fixed in citations. Table of contents verified against the OUP catalogue: Preface; Part I, Early India (1 General Background; 2 Quintum Non Datur; 3 Well-Founded Metaphysics); Part II, Later India (4 Emptiness; 5 The Fifth Corner; 6 Paradox and Ineffability); Part III, East Asia (7 And So On; 8 The Golden Lion; 9 Enlightenment); 10 A Methodological Coda. The book has not yet been acquired; every quotation below is transcribed from published reviews (Westerhoff in *Mind*, Siderits in NDPR, Green in *Journal of Buddhist Ethics*) and awaits collation against the printed pages.

## Source scholarship

The book narrates a single formal idea across a millennium of Buddhist philosophy. The catuṣkoṭi's four corners — true, false, both, neither — are read as the four values of First Degree Entailment, constructed as subsets of {T, F}: {T}, {F}, {T, F}, and {}. That gives the early tradition's fourfold scheme an exact non-classical semantics in which "both" and "neither" are values in good standing rather than confusions. Chapter 2's title, "Quintum Non Datur," names the thesis that there is no fifth possibility — and names it precisely so the book can break it. When Nāgārjuna rejects all four corners (Priest's anchor texts include MMK XXII:11 and XXV:17), Priest introduces a fifth value, e, for the ineffable. Crucially, e is not an extension of the FDE lattice: it stands outside the order entirely, and it is infectious — any compound with an e-valued component is itself e-valued (e-in/e-out). The apparent self-refutation of speaking about the ineffable is then handled by plurivalent semantics, in which evaluation is a relation rather than a function, so a single claim can bear more than one value — true and ineffable at once.

The East Asian chapters carry the construction forward. Jizang's hierarchy of the two truths iterates the pair: each level's distinction between conventional and ultimate becomes, at the next level, merely conventional — the process Priest titles "And So On," an unbounded ascent in which every articulated ultimate is demoted the moment it is articulated. Dōgen arrives as the narrative's convergence point — "a focal point of all the rays of our narrative" (p. 142, via Westerhoff's review) — where ineffability and enlightenment practice meet. The methodological coda asks whether the anachronism is vicious and answers it directly: "Would the actors in the drama of this book have used those insights and tools had they been available to them? I see no reason why not." (p. 149, via reviews). Priest is candid about the book's register: it "is not a scholarly work" (p. xvii) and does not claim to be "an authoritative textual and historical interpretation" (p. xviii). The essay must quote him at his own estimate.

### Reception and gates

This house is gated: no use of Priest's construction may pass into the essay without clearing the published objections.

- **Siderits (NDPR):** offers a rival presupposition-failure reading — all four lemmas are rejected because they share a false presupposition, and no non-classical logic is needed to say so. If Siderits is right, the fifth value is machinery without a job.
- **Westerhoff (*Mind*):** the catuṣkoṭi is not uniform across contexts, so no single formal treatment can be the logic of the tetralemma; parsimony favors classical readings where they suffice; and a passage Priest attributes to Candrakīrti (p. 58) is in fact from the nineteenth-century Mipham — a dating error of some seven centuries that the essay must not reproduce.
- **Green (*Journal of Buddhist Ethics*):** the tradition reads the tetralemma as refuting all positions, a reified "ineffable" included; hypostasizing ineffability as a value is exactly the move the texts warn against.
- **Kapsner ("Cutting Corners," *Comparative Philosophy* 11.2, 2020; see [[symbolon/episteme/sources/mathematics-logic/kapsner/kapsner-2020-cutting-corners/kapsner-2020-cutting-corners.md|kapsner-2020-cutting-corners]]):** the friendliest logician's objection — the fifth value specifically is rejected on internal grounds, and an alternative account without it is sketched.

The essay's use survives these gates for a stated reason: QL's #0 is a generative precondition, not a truth-value. Every published objection targets e's standing *as a value*; none touches a ground that was never a value in the first place. That is the exact joint at which the essay's reading and Priest's part company, and it must be stated wherever this house is cited.

## Essay use

### Source's relevant contribution

Priest's book is the fullest formal narrative of the catuṣkoṭi from FDE through the fifth value to Jizang and Dōgen — the arc the essay reads as the tradition's own performance of the return that the value-theory cannot write.

### Licensed essay use

- Carry the FDE reading of the four corners and the arrival of e as the formal counterpart of QL's four explicit positions and its ground #0.
- Use Jizang's iterated hierarchy and Dōgen's convergence as the tradition performing the 5→0 return that Priest's formalism reaches only as silence.
- Cite the methodological coda and Priest's own disclaimers to frame the book's register honestly.
- State explicitly, wherever the fifth value is invoked, that QL's #0 is a precondition and not a value, and cite the reception gates.

### Claim boundary

Priest's construction is not settled history of the catuṣkoṭi; the reception above contests both the formal need for e and the historical uniformity of the tetralemma. The essay may not present the five-valued reading as the scholarly consensus, may not repeat the Candrakīrti/Mipham misattribution, and may not claim Priest for QL's ground — the identification of e's arrival with an arrival *at* #0 is the essay's own Argued move.

^priest-2018-fifth-corner-q002
